Zoe

the Aspect of Twilight
Mid laneSupport lane

Zoe support turns bot lane into a shooting range. From behind your ADC, you poke with long Paddle Stars and catch enemies with Sleepy Trouble Bubble, setting up kills your ADC can follow. It's a niche, high-risk pick: unlike tank supports she can't protect her carry well, but a good Zoe support decides fights before they begin.

When to pick Zoe

✗ Better as a counter-pick

Not safe to blind pick: hard-engage supports can kill her before she acts.

Pick into

  • Immobile enchanter or mage supports like Seraphine and Lux
  • Roaming supports who leave their ADC alone, like Bard
  • Squishy enemy ADCs you can burst from range
  • Enemy bot lanes without hard engage

Avoid into

  • Hard-engage supports like Leona and Alistar
  • Tanky supports with brush control like Maokai
  • Teams with lots of divers who'll reach your ADC
  • Situations where your ADC needs a protector, not a poker

Great teammates

Miss FortuneHer damage follows up perfectly on sleeping targets.
XayahHer root combos with your bubble for easy kills.
LuxTwo long-range poke threats make bot lane unplayable for the enemy.

Your team needs: Pick Zoe support when your team has enough frontline and your ADC can play safely without heavy peel.

How to read the enemy team → · Practice drafting →

Strengths

  • Huge poke and burst from very long range, even with support items
  • Sleep bubble sets up kills for your ADC, especially from the brush
  • Long-range pick potential when roaming with your jungler
  • Spell Thief: extra summoners and items to pick up in fights

Weaknesses

  • Very squishy: hard-engage supports can kill you before you act
  • Can't peel well: if a diver reaches your ADC, you can only bubble or poke
  • Relies on landing skill shots: misses leave your ADC on their own
  • Less vision-focused tools than enchanter supports

Power spikes

  • Level 2: E + Q gives you a strong kill threat with your ADC
  • Support item upgrades: World Atlas finishes into Zaz'Zak's Realmspike for extra poke damage
  • First item (Imperial Mandate): your bubble and slows mark enemies for bonus damage from your team
  • Two items (Horizon Focus): long-range Qs deal even more damage
  • Level 6: Portal Jump makes it much harder for engage supports to catch you

Top tips

  • Use the brush: bubbles from unseen angles are much harder to dodge
  • Pick up every dropped Flash or Heal with W
  • Ping your ADC before you go for a bubble
  • Stay behind your ADC; you can't survive engages
  • Use cheap control wards from your support quest
  • Poke before objectives so the enemy can't contest
  • Pair with ADCs who have high burst follow-up
